intro: Le deuxième conditionnel (If I had more time, I would travel) parle de situations imaginaires, improbables ou contraires à la réalité présente, et de leurs conséquences. C'est l'équivalent de « si + imparfait, conditionnel » en français, et il sert aussi à donner des conseils et à parler poliment.
objectifs: Construire le deuxième conditionnel avec if + prétérit et would + base verbale.
Distinguer une situation réelle et probable (premier conditionnel) d'une situation imaginaire ou improbable (deuxième conditionnel).
Utiliser If I were you… pour conseiller, et were à toutes les personnes dans un registre soigné.
Nuancer le résultat avec could et might, et poser des questions hypothétiques (What would you do if…?).

texte: Condition : if + prétérit (simple ou continu). Résultat : would + base verbale. Contraction : 'd (I'd, she'd) ; négation : wouldn't. Même règle de virgule qu'au premier conditionnel.

Le prétérit ici ne parle pas du passé : il marque la distance avec la réalité. « If I had a car » = je n'ai pas de voiture (maintenant). C'est exactement comme l'imparfait français dans « si j'avais une voiture ».

lignes: we would see her more often.

sections.note: Comme pour will, would ne va jamais dans la partie en if : « If I would have money » est faux.

sections.titre: Réel ou imaginaire ? Premier ou deuxième conditionnel
texte: Le choix dépend de la façon dont le locuteur voit la situation. Premier conditionnel : c'est possible, réaliste. Deuxième conditionnel : c'est imaginaire, peu probable ou impossible.
« If I win the match, I'll be happy » (je suis un bon joueur, c'est possible). « If I won the lottery, I'd stop working » (rêve, très improbable).
exemples: If I get the job, I'll move to Lille.
If I got a job in Japan, I'd learn Japanese.
If I were taller, I'd play basketball.
Impossible à changer : situation contraire à la réalité.
What would you do if you saw a lion in the street?

sections.titre: « If I were… » et les conseils
texte: Avec be, on peut utiliser were à toutes les personnes : If I were, if he were, if it were. C'est la forme recommandée à l'écrit et à l'examen. Was (if I was, if she was) est courant à l'oral mais moins soigné.
« If I were you, I'd… » (à ta place, je…) est la façon classique de donner un conseil. Dans cette expression figée, on garde toujours were.
exemples: If I were you, I'd apologise.
If it were cheaper, more people would buy it.
I wouldn't sign that contract if I were you.

texte: Dans le résultat, could = would be able to (pourrait), might = would perhaps (pourrait peut-être). Dans la condition, could = was able to : « If I could drive, I'd help you move. »
Les questions hypothétiques sont très utiles en conversation et dans les entretiens : What would you do if…? Where would you live if…? Réponse courte : Yes, I would. / No, I wouldn't.

lignes: If I had time, I would help you.
If I had a car, I could drive you home.
If you asked him nicely, he might say yes.
If I could speak Dutch, I'd apply for that job in Ghent.

sections.titre: La politesse et les situations délicates
texte: Le deuxième conditionnel adoucit une demande ou une proposition : « Would it be OK if I left early today? », « It would be great if you could send me the file. » La distance grammaticale crée une distance polie.
Il sert aussi à refuser gentiment : « I'd love to come, but… » et à parler de principes : « I would never lie to a friend. »
exemples: Would you mind if I opened the window?
It would be helpful if you arrived ten minutes early.

formule: If + prétérit, would / could / might + base verbale (If I had time, I'd help you. · If I were you, I'd…)
prononciation: 'd est presque inaudible : « I'd go » /aɪd ɡəʊ/. Écoute le léger /d/ qui distingue « I go » de « I'd go ». Devant une voyelle il se lie : « I'd ask » /aɪˈdɑːsk/.
would est faible dans une question : « What would you do? » /ˈwɒt wəd jə ˈduː/ ; souvent « wouldja » /ˈwʊdʒə/ à l'oral rapide.
wouldn't /ˈwʊdnt/ : le l ne se prononce pas (comme dans could et should).
were est faible /wə/ dans « If I were you » : /ɪf aɪ wə ˈjuː/, avec l'accent sur you.
Intonation montante sur la condition, descendante sur le résultat, comme au premier conditionnel.
erreurs: If I would have more time, I would travel.
If I had more time, I would travel.
Pas de would dans la partie en if : prétérit.
If I had money, I will buy a car.
If I had money, I would buy a car.
Prétérit dans la condition → would dans le résultat (pas will).
If I am you, I would accept.
If I were you, I would accept.
Expression figée : If I were you.
If I would be rich, I would help my family.
If I were rich, I would help my family.
What you would do if you lost your job?
What would you do if you lost your job?
If I could, I would to help you.
If I could, I would help you.

dialogue.contexte: Abidjan, à la terrasse d'un café. Awa et son ami Pierre, en visite depuis Québec, imaginent une autre vie.
lignes: What would you do if you didn't have to work?
Que ferais-tu si tu n'avais pas besoin de travailler ?
I'd open a small restaurant by the sea. And you?
J'ouvrirais un petit restaurant au bord de la mer. Et toi ?
If I had the money, I'd travel around Africa for a year.
Si j'avais l'argent, je voyagerais en Afrique pendant un an.
You could start with Ghana. It isn't far from here.
Tu pourrais commencer par le Ghana. Ce n'est pas loin d'ici.
True. But if I left my job, my boss would be furious!
C'est vrai. Mais si je quittais mon travail, mon patron serait furieux !
If I were you, I'd ask for unpaid leave.
À ta place, je demanderais un congé sans solde.
That's a good idea. He might accept if I asked him early.
Bonne idée. Il accepterait peut-être si je lui demandais tôt.
And if you came back next year, you could eat at my restaurant!
Et si tu revenais l'année prochaine, tu pourrais manger dans mon restaurant !

mots: Imagine you lived on an island.
If I could afford it, I'd buy a bigger flat.
What would you do if you won the lottery?
If I were you, I'd apologise.
Can I give you some advice?
She took unpaid leave to travel.
Would you mind if I sat here?
In my dream life, I'd live by the sea.

exercices.consigne: Choisis la forme qui convient au sens indiqué.
items: (Possible) If it (rains / rained) tomorrow, we'll cancel the picnic.
rains
(Imaginaire) If I (am / were) a bird, I'd fly to Cameroon.
were
(Imaginaire) If she (has / had) wings, she would fly.
had
(Possible) If you (call / called) me tonight, I'll explain.
call

exercices.consigne: Mets les verbes à la bonne forme (deuxième conditionnel).
items: If I ___ (know) her number, I ___ (call) her.
knew … would call ('d call)
We ___ (not / live) here if we ___ (have) a choice.
wouldn't live … had
If he ___ (be) more patient, he ___ (be) a good teacher.
were (was) … would be
What ___ you ___ (do) if you ___ (lose) your passport abroad?
would … do … lost
If they ___ (can) speak French, they ___ (move) to Quebec.
could … would move

exercices.consigne: Réécris la phrase au deuxième conditionnel pour imaginer le contraire.
items: I don't have a car, so I can't drive you home.
If I had a car, I could drive you home.
She's very busy, so she doesn't call her parents.
If she weren't (wasn't) so busy, she would call her parents.
We don't speak Dutch, so we don't understand the signs.
If we spoke Dutch, we would understand the signs.
It's raining, so we aren't going to the beach.
If it weren't (wasn't) raining, we would go to the beach.

exercices.consigne: Chaque phrase contient une erreur. Corrige-la.
items: If I would win the lottery, I would buy a house.
If I won the lottery, I would buy a house.
If I am you, I would talk to her.
If I were you, I would talk to her.
If she had time, she will help us.
If she had time, she would help us.
What you would say if he asked you?
What would you say if he asked you?
Si j'avais plus de temps, j'apprendrais le piano.
If I had more time, I would learn the piano.
À ta place, je ne dirais rien.
If I were you, I wouldn't say anything.
Que ferais-tu si tu habitais à Bruxelles ?
What would you do if you lived in Brussels?
Ça vous dérangerait si je partais plus tôt ?
Would you mind if I left earlier?

exercices.consigne: Réponds en 4 phrases à la question : « What would you do if you could live anywhere in the world? » Utilise would, could et might.
items: Exemple de réponse

If I could live anywhere, I'd choose Vancouver. I would live near the mountains and go hiking every weekend. I could also work from home for a company in Europe. My family might visit me every summer.

a_retenir: If + prétérit, would + base verbale : situation imaginaire ou improbable (présent ou futur).
Le prétérit marque la distance avec la réalité, pas le passé.
Jamais would dans la partie en if.
If I were you, I'd… pour conseiller ; were possible à toutes les personnes.
